prompt: A realistic 1920s photograph on grainy colour film: real people with real skin, pores and stubble, in real places. Seen straight down from the ceiling, the scene is folded into six mirrored segments round a centre point, as if looked at through a brass kaleidoscope, the mirror seams crisp straight lines, each segment the same real photograph repeated so the whole frame becomes a gold-and-black star. The scene: a hidden basement print room where gangsters in pinstripe suits shovel coal into printing presses and sheets of banknotes fly up, and at the exact centre a tall skinny man in a bowler hat with a heavy gold mayoral chain round his neck, a long narrow face, hollow cheeks and a pencil-thin grey moustache dances with his arms flung out. Light: hanging brass lamps and the red-hot fireboxes; deep shadow between them. Plain margins with no writing. Thanks.
